Tech Report: Super subs, xG kings and $150 million question marks: The Premier League's most intriguing players

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 11 min read (2299 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~11 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life.
  • Industry observers note that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions.
  • Recent findings suggest that spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Whatever you might think about the November international break, there is one fact you simply will not be bothered to argue against: it is well timed for the statistically-minded football fan in your life. A 10-game sample size -- that's the useful stuff. At this point, many but not all teams are what their analytics tell us they are. It's similar but not quite the same for players. Not many have hit the 900-minute mark yet, but plenty are at 500-plus, a body of evidence that usually isn't warped by any one good or bad game. Of course, it depends on how good or bad that game is.

Industry observers note that we are not yet, then, at the stage where we can always draw hard and fast conclusions. We are, however, in a position to find some interesting questions. Here are five of them, in player form:.

Recent findings suggest that spend $100 million on a player who turns 29 next week and the expectation is surely that a player will hit the ground running. That's especially true when they're Bruno Guimaraes, terror of Premier League midfields in a Newcastle United shirt, a player who had long since seemed ready to step up to a Champions League contender. While it would be fair to say that the Brazilian's form is nothing like a problem for table-topping Arsenal, he has not exactly started like a house on fire. Mikel Arteta has acknowledged as much whenever he has spoken about Guimaraes, even when served up the opportunity to praise him after what seemed an impressive performance against Hull City.

"He's hitting serious levels now, but we can still take him to another level. That's my conviction; I told him that in the dressing room -- he owned a lot of moments in the game, but there is still much more to come." It would be fair to say that, Hull aside, the best levels he has hit have been as a substitute. When he comes off the bench, he passes more accurately, wins more tackles, creates chances and scores brilliant goals. As a starter, he has occasionally looked a beat off his teammates.

It has been revealed that physical data from Gradient Sports hints as to what the issue might be. For every 90 Premier League minutes on the field, Guimaraes covers less of it at sprint speed (≥25 km/h) than any outfield player bar Mikel Merino and spends notably more time jogging than anyone, an average of 30 minutes. Compare Guimaraes to Declan Rice, an admittedly vertiginous bar, and it is easy to see why the upcoming guy looks off the pace.

Recent findings suggest that equally, it explains why he's such a compelling substitute. When the other 21 players on the pitch are flagging, Guimaraes' comparative physical complications go unexposed and he can run the show.

That's all well and good for now, but he can't carry on like this, can he? You would have to assume that Myles Lewis-Skelly will have to make way even if the academy graduate's emergence as a midfield option unlocked an improved Declan Rice at the tail end of last season. The second most expensive signing in your history can't be an impact guy off the bench behind the homegrown kid, right? Probably not, but if there's any team that could justify the idea of Guimaraes as a 12th man, maybe it's Arsenal, where they pride themselves on their game-changing finishers.

Recent findings suggest that erling Haaland's Swiftian reign at the top of the Premier League xG chart has been interrupted, at least temporarily, by an unlikely source. You'd have to go back to the days of a marauding Romelu Lukaku for the last time an Everton striker looked like they might rule the roost. Only once since the Belgian's departure has an Evertonian cleared 20 goals in all competitions. In the last five, even a dozen has been beyond this club.

According to recent reports, thierno Barry isn't there yet, but boy is he on the right trajectory. His 7.28 non-penalty expected goals (npxG) puts him 0.22 ahead of Haaland and nearly 2.5 npxG up on anyone else in the league. Expand the pool to Europe's top five leagues and he is breathing rarefied air behind the top four of Lamine Yamal, Donyell Malen, Raphinha and Kylian Mbappe, all of whom have the advantage that they are not playing for an upper midtable outfit in the continent's most competitive division. And in that environment, Barry is making the hardest thing in the sport look easy: getting good shots in prime locations.

If Barry were turning them in as often as he was getting them, Everton might be even higher than sixth. Still, six goals through 10 games is not to be sniffed at, particularly when the pressure on the 24-year-old was so intense. The bungling of a deadline-day move for Folarin Balogun, as Beto moved to Fiorentina, meant it was Barry or bust for David Moyes this season.

Perhaps it was an enforced show of faith for a player who was in and out of the XI last season, his first in England, that brought the best out of the former Villarreal man. His manager views the success in more straightforward terms. "He has settled down a bit more," mentioned Moyes after Barry's brace helped down Coventry. "His language, his understanding, his communication is much better and he has worked hard to get himself in those positions to score.".

Recent findings suggest that it is easy to see why getting the soft factors right might have been all that was required. Barry is the ideal striker for the modern Premier League. Tall, strong and mobile -- he ranks third among center forwards for top speed this season, per Gradient Sports -- he can serve as an outball when a press needs beating and then get in the box. He might not have the technical elegance of an Mbappe, but he makes his presence felt and occupies high-value spaces. That is more valuable than it sounds, as proven when James Tarkowski's howitzer from range deflected in off him. You might not like it, but this is what elite center forward play looks like. Long may it continue, at least as far as Everton are concerned.

Sources indicate that there are three types of underrated footballers. First, your common-or-garden-variety underrated footballers, often to be found plying their trade at Wolverhampton Wanderers or Burnley. Ashley Westwood, in that season, put up stupidly high xA numbers. Then there are the so-often-dubbed-underrated that they actually become a bit overrated. Leighton Baines. Lee Carsley. They don't have to play for Everton, but it does help. Olivier Giroud is another. See, not all Everton.

Recent findings suggest that the most rarely spotted of the underrated is the chameleonic one, correctly pegged for a while, only to develop to the point that he is underrated in a completely different way to how he once was. Take Alex Iwobi. Some time ago, a consensus coalesced around the Nigeria international that he was a good player for a team at Fulham's level (and indeed Everton's). Any minute he was on the field, he would probably be delivering good performances for good Premier League teams.

Recent findings suggest that not anymore. Ten games in and Iwobi looks like one of the outstanding creative forces in the Premier League, critical to the march towards adequacy that Fulham have undertaken after a slow start to life with Alvaro Arbeloa.

It has been revealed that among true playmakers, Iwobi is one of the best at getting the ball into dangerous areas and creating for his teammates. Iwobi leads the league in expected assists with 2.95 and is tied with Bruno Fernandes for most passes completed into the penalty area. Only Pascal Gross has created more chances.

Those players can't match Iwobi when it comes to ball progression either. In terms of advancing the ball not just into the box but from deeper, Fulham's ball-playing fulcrum on the inside left channel has completed more progressive passes than anyone not named Declan Rice or Jan Paul van Hecke.

Sources indicate that when Iwobi broke through at Arsenal, he displayed a preternatural sense for how to keep attacks alive, the pass before the pass before the pass. Now a 30-year-old, Iwobi still does that more than he unpicks defenses. One cannot argue, however, that he is not putting his teammates in the right spot. It is just that not everyone quite appreciates how often he does so just yet, including his own supporters, who jeered Iwobi when he was substituted in the early-season defeat to Crystal Palace. Since then, he has responded to his critics in style, teeing up two or more shots in each of Fulham's last seven Premier League matches. If a few more of them had been converted, in fact, if any of them had been converted, then Iwobi might not still be underrated.

According to recent reports, the upper reaches of the list of most expensive transfers of all time are hardly all bangers all the time, but of the biggest money moves in the sport's history there are only a handful where at such an early stage you find yourself wondering if anyone really understood what the plan was. Manchester City committed the best part of $150 million on Enzo Fernandez this summer, a fee only eclipsed by Neymar and Kylian Mbappe. Beyond a vague sense that it would be nice to give newly introduced manager Enzo Maresca one of his favorite players, what was it they had in mind?

We pointed out earlier in the season that the aggressive positioning of Fernandez in the 5-3 win over Sunderland looked extreme; at the time it seemed reasonable to view it as a reflection of a stretched-out, chaotic game. Maresca had, of course, unlocked more number 10-ish qualities in the Argentine at Chelsea, but surely that had been reflective of what that team needed, particularly as Cole Palmer went off the boil? Perhaps not. Fernandez keeps popping up in the sort of positions that leave Elliot Anderson on an island. It is one thing to view Anderson as the fresh Rodri, quite another to immediately throw the England international in at the deep end, tying a whole midfield together by force of will.

Of course you could sketch out a logic for why you might push Fernandez high. It is not so long ago that City deployed two playmakers in front of a sitting midfielder and they ruled the Premier League. Fernandez and Rayan Cherki aren't Kevin De Bruyne and David Silva though.

Maybe Cherki could be offering a level of creation on a par with City greats; he started well enough last season. In year two, he is creating lower-quality chances, his expected assists per 90 dropping by 50%, notably more than the slight uptick in the quality and quantity of shots he is taking. It's no surprise that Cherki is creating less when fewer of his touches are coming in the attacking third. The output has been there so far, five goals and two assists in nine Premier League games, but for that to continue, Maresca might want to be getting his No. 10 into more dangerous spots.

According to recent reports, instead, those seem to be going to Fernandez, who has not proven himself able to get the final-third production to justify his platforming. For every 100 touches he takes, he is delivering significantly less npxG+xA than in either of the previous two seasons. Meanwhile, he is less effective without the ball than he has been at any stage since coming to England. That's no wonder. If an opponent passes through City's frontline, then Fernandez does not have the mobility to get back.

As such, to enable themselves to get perhaps a shot or two more than they would get with Ayyoub Bouaddi or Mateo Kovacic next to Anderson, City have made themselves an even more vulnerable side to the counterattack, already giving up more fast-break openings than they did in 2020-21 or 2021-22. Carry on like this, and Fernandez will become one of those nine-figure transfers, the ones that live in infamy.

Sources indicate that it was a signing that delighted a city when it was announced in early August, and rightly so. Loaning Carl Rushworth from Brighton had been an inspired bit of business by Coventry City, the then-24-year-old goalkeeper anchoring the best defense in the division as Frank Lampard's side returned to the top flight for the first time in over a quarter of a century. A club-record £22 million fee seemed a snip for such a young talent.

In a recent development, all of that is worth bearing in mind given the struggles Rushworth has endured this season: saving just 53.7% of shots he has faced, conceding 5.19 more goals than the xG value of the shots he has faced. The swagger of last season has been replaced by a sloppiness apparent in both the goals he conceded in the second half against Tottenham, weak gloves doing nothing to repel efforts that came at him a bit quicker and a bit sooner than they might have last year.

Sources indicate that none of this needs to be a problem for Rushworth. In 2023-24, James Trafford was another highly touted young goalkeeper afforded a shot at the big time by Burnley. He was obliterated up and down the Premier League, his first touch in the division picking the ball out of the net off Erling Haaland. Those struggles were the making of him, as they have broken others. It'll be some time yet before we discover which way these past few months send Rushworth.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

LATEST YORK – The awkward logistics of Sunday's NWSL semifinal at Icahn Stadium, a quirky little venue sandwiched on an island in between Manhattan and Queens, were supposed to give way once Gotham FC and the Kansas City Current took to the pitch for one of the league's showpiece matches. When the Current's Croix Bethune opened the scoring in the 20th minute with an incredible looping shot off a free kick, the theme of the day was in motion. The league would make the best of the unideal circumstances with a top-quality soccer game, or at least with a few highlight-reel moments nestled into a match contested by a collection of the world's most talented players.

"I've been working on free kicks all year," Bethune remarked post-match, the Current justified in their decision to sign her last winter even if the validation was no longer needed, "and a lot more leading into the playoffs so just practice makes perfect.".

In a recent development, icahn Stadium's irregularities, though, seemed to reflect the game it unexpectedly became the host of six days earlier. The Current's 2-1 win came courtesy of a chippy game plan that would have been the case if the match had taken place at a traditional soccer-specific stadium but it felt especially at home at Icahn Stadium and amidst its elements. The teams played against the wind during Newly introduced York's first properly cold weekend of the season, and Gotham faced a setting sun that impacted their vision during the first half. Bethune's impressive strike was really the only on-field spectacle to be witnessed on Randall's Island.

BEND IT LIKE BETHUNE 💫 KC takes the lead!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/F4mQePT5QJ.

"We knew it was going to be a physical game, without a doubt," Current forward Haley Hopkins stated. "Like I said a million times, Gotham's a very, very good team and so we had to be super disciplined in our structure and catch them on their transition and we were just able to put the ball in the back of the net when we had our opportunities.".

It has been revealed that the introduction of Gotham's Rose Lavelle, who has been dealing with niggling fitness challenges over the last few weeks, did not change the smash-and-grab energy of the game. Much as there was a week ago in their quarterfinal win over the Seattle Reign, there was a dull quality to Gotham's attack despite their star power. Over 180 minutes of possession play, the NWSL Shield winners managed zero shots on target and 0.66 expected goals, their midseason marquee signing Sam Kerr managing no shots along the way and mustering just one attempt in her last five matches. To say they were unlucky would be a stretch but their lively start to the second half gave their failed attempts to put a shot on frame a comedic feel.

"I think we were kind of our own worst enemy today," midfielder Savannah McCaskill mentioned. "I think at times we played into what they wanted to do and their style of play. They want a very chippy game. They want to get into tackles. They want to draw fouls. They want to break up the game. They want to play long and that's not our style. We want to keep the ball. We want to control tempo, and we like to play pretty football. That's [what] we pride ourselves on … but I think we need to find a better way to balance that out, especially in this league. How can we meet the demand of a chippy game while also controlling the tempo? I think we did a really good job when we played them at home the last time [a 2-1 win on Aug. 14]. They scored early but then we completely dominated the rest of the game and I think we failed to do that today and so I think that's really the determining factor.".

In other words, it was the perfect setup for Gotham to equalize off an own goal from Laney Rouse, a week after benefiting from another own goal from the Reign's Jordyn Bugg. Those two goals would be the only ones in their postseason run, just as one might expect from the NWSL Shield winners and reigning champions who entered the playoffs as the favorites to win another title.

Gotham FC find a way to tie up the semifinal 💪NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/Itbzs4Bhz1.

Recent findings suggest that gotham goalkeeper Ann-Katrin Berger then slipped into game-saving mode with two important blocks while defender Tierna Davidson did what she could to hold the Current at bay, attempting to create a villain arc rivaled only by Argentina's run to the World Cup final. Though the hosts had lucked their way into an even game by the 88th minute, the dark and cold conditions at a downsized stadium in an obscure part of Newly introduced York meant the game beckoned for extra time. One final smash and grab was undoubtedly in the cards, though where it would come from was hard to guess – the Current had put in the work to win but soccer's chaotic nature had already weaseled its way into the game.

Industry observers note that in the end, it was the Current's Haley Hopkins who had the final say in the 89th minute off of – what else – a set piece, a free kick that led the forward to finally evade Berger with a shot off the crossbar. After losing to them twice in three previous meetings this season, the Current earned their spot in next week's NWSL Championship (Saturday, 8 p.m. ET, CBS, Paramount+) on the back of a well-executed gameplan.

HALEY HOPKINS CLUTCH OFF THE CROSSBAR 🤯The KC Current lead 2-1!NWSL Playoffs presented by Google Pixel pic.twitter.com/BT2OZhwX1y.

Sources indicate that "As much as we tried to analyze certain teams in the league that have given them trouble, we really took information from the games we've played against them, all the ways they challenged us," Current head coach Chris Armas said. "There's been games even where they get high [expected goals], too much progression, too much in our box and we just tried to then look at all the scenes and moments when we made it hard for them so we just tried to take from yesterday and apply it to today, [that] type of thing. We gave up zero shots on goal in 90 minutes. The commitment from our players to just will themselves to it to stick to a match blueprint that was going to be largely about taking away spaces, controlling the middle of the pitch and if we can do that on the day – and and we did that by running after them, too, and pressing in moments of high intensity – we not only might stop what they're trying to do on one end and maybe force the turnovers that could challenge them so a little bit of a chess match there in moments.".

The Current were no slouches, finishing fourth in the regular season and now on a  seven-game winning streak en route to next week's championship. Bethune's star quality shone on Sunday, while the team's record with two-time NWSL MVP Temwa Chawinga and U.S. women's national team standout Michelle Cooper is formidable. It did not erase the fact that they slayed a giant along the way, knocking out the Shield winners and a team that had picked up five major titles in four seasons.

"Gotham has just raised the bar around the league and in our country here, so the way they play, the way the coach sets them up, the talent on the team, the type of games they can put you in, you have to come with a blueprint," Armas remarked. "They're a team that, again, if iron sharpens iron type of thing, we try to push teams and we try to raise the bar.".

Gotham, though, had not looked the part of the NWSL's gold standard team. Their drastic run, while presently headlined by USWNT players Lavelle and Jaedyn Shaw, is built on the back of an effective defensive structure that has carried an inconsistent offense. Lavelle and, in particular, Shaw have picked up much of the slack en route to the NWSL Shield and Kerr was supposed to bolster their attack after Esther Gonzalez's shock departure for Saudi club Al Qadsiah. They finished the regular season sixth in the NWSL for expected goals with 49.01 but had a genuine finishing problem, notching just 39 goals and ranking in the league's bottom six in that category. Head coach Juan Carlos Amoros is not sounding the alarm just yet but as they enter another offseason, the attacking composition of the team deserves yet another look.

It has been revealed that "Of course, we want to create more chances, more shots," Amoros said. "We all do but we look at the way we play. We look at the way we create chances. We look at who does that. I think when it comes to these games, could we have [made] some better decisions? Yes, we did. We actually create some good moments. Yes, I wouldn't over-think about it. Something that I'm happy [about]? No but at the same time, we work a lot to make sure that those moments happen. So you know the set pieces, those situations, the open plays, final decisions … Definitely, something that we want to be better [at]. We want to score more goals. I think that we are the best team defending in the league with our aggressive approach to defending but we want to also be able to create and score more goals.".

More importantly, though, Gotham were not treated like the bar-raising team they have become over the years. Icahn Stadium has its charms and is a worthy inclusion on the list of wacky and wonderful places that embody American soccer, an enjoyably chaotic slice of the world's most popular game. It was also a back-up initiative for a team that has called Sports Illustrated Stadium home for five years, settling in nicely to a state-of-the-art soccer-specific build for MLS' Red Bull Upcoming York that can hold 20,000 more fans than the 5,000-seater Icahn Stadium can. The pitch at Sports Illustrated Stadium, managed by RBNY, had fallen into disrepair and with the primary tenants' end-of-season friendly scheduled for the night before, there was not enough time to fix it. The quirks of Icahn Stadium only served as a reminder that Gotham – and the NWSL – should not have actually been there, even if the field at Randall's Island was better suited for the occasion.

In a recent development, "I want to be really clear and direct in saying that in these types of situations, the field is never an excuse," winger Midge Purce said. "We lost today because we weren't the better team. That being said, I would say it's inexcusable. It's not what you want in a professional league. It's not what you want for women who are progressing in the United States and supposed to be one of the best leagues in the entire world. I think it's a bad look for everyone involved and we always want to be at Sports Illustrated [Stadium] in front of our fans when we earned that right throughout the season but I would say it had no effect on performance today.".

Industry observers note that the Current's trip to Icahn Stadium is not where the NWSL's efforts to make lemonade end, either. Saturday's semifinal, in which the Washington Spirit beat the Utah Royals to book their spot in a championship game at their home of Audi Field, only added to it. One of the Spirit's sponsors underwrote the costs to push the start time of the Secretaries' Cup, a Division III football game, by a few hours but both matches were played on a field with soccer and football lines. The football lines will likely be faint but visible for next week's NWSL Championship, while the playability of the actual field will probably face a few questions in the build-up.

"I think we will never know what happened if we would have played [at Sports Illustrated Stadium] on a good pitch," Amoros said. "I think it was the right decision to come here. I think the pitch in the other stadium was unfortunately unplayable under our view. The last couple of games we picked up injuries. Luckily, nothing that has been a season-ending injury but we have to protect our players and guarantee the quality of football so to thank the club, obviously.

According to recent reports, "Overall, I think it's been a sad weekend. I think also the situation in Washington yesterday. This league deserves better. The two, arguably, best teams, [most] consistent, having to deal with these situations and then yesterday, you sit down to watch that game around the world and you're seeing those American football lines across today. Credit to the club and the fans. I think they've done an amazing job here. The fans welcomed us. The club has really shifted everything to play here but we couldn't play in our ground where we could have had more people, where we are unbeaten in 13 games at the moment and but I think we took that decision, putting players' safety first, and the outcome is the outcome.".

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Sources indicate that julián Álvarez created both of Atlético Madrid's first-half goals as the visitors ended Getafe's unbeaten home league record this season. Atlético now sit two points behind Real Madrid, while Getafe are left one point above the relegation zone before the midweek European games.

Both of Atlético’s first-half goals in this matchday 13 LaLiga fixture came inside the opening 30 minutes.

Recent findings suggest that álex Baena opened the scoring in the 10th minute with a low, powerful shot from outside the area. It was his sixth LaLiga goal of the season. Johnny Cardoso doubled the lead on 30 minutes when David Soria missed a punch at a corner. It was Cardoso’s first league goal for Atlético.

Recent findings suggest that getafe finished with ten men. VAR confirmed a penalty involving Alexander Sørloth in the 89th minute. Dakonam Ortega Djené was then sent off in the 90th minute, having been booked in the 71st. Álex Grimaldo converted the penalty in the second minute of stoppage time for his fifth goal of the league campaign. About 10,000 spectators watched the game, according to Telemadrid.

According to recent reports, the visitors had 68% of the ball and completed 652 accurate passes to Getafe’s 238. They took 20 shots to the hosts’ 11. Getafe’s goalkeeper made 7 saves, while Jan Oblak needed to make only 1.

Álvarez played 75 minutes and created 4 key passes. Baena was rated 8.2 and Cardoso 8.13. Diego Simeone was without Ademola Lookman, Marc Pubill and Cristian ‘Cuti’ Romero for the trip.

Industry observers note that the win followed two straight defeats for Atlético, 1-2 against Barcelona and 0-2 against Bayern München. It also followed last season’s 0-1 Atlético win at the Coliseum on 23 November 2025.

Barcelona lead the table on 36 points, with Real Madrid second on 33.

It has been revealed that pepe Bordalás’s side went into the game having lost every away league match without scoring. They had conceded 14 goals on the road.

#FINAL | Derrota.@GetafeCF 0⃣-3⃣ @Atleti #GetafeAtleti pic.twitter.com/lCpJZ8dHws.

— Getafe C.F. (@GetafeCF) November 22, 2026.

It has been revealed that getafe have lost their last three games in all competitions, against Brighton, Villarreal and Atlético. They sit 17th with 12 points and a goal difference of -13. Levante are 18th on 11 points and Elche 19th on 10, both with a game in hand. Getafe could fall into the relegation zone if Levante or Elche win their games on Monday, VAVEL España reported.

Recent findings suggest that atlético return to action on Wednesday 25 November against Viking at the Metropolitano. That game is matchday 5 of the Champions League league phase, and both sides have four points going into it. Getafe travel to FC Iberia 1999 in the UEFA Conference League on Thursday 26 November.

💡 Key Takeaways
  • Three days after tearing up as he confirmed his departure from the U.S.
  • Industry observers note that after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity.
  • "For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Three days after tearing up as he confirmed his departure from the U.S. men's national team, outgoing head coach Mauricio Pochettino said he does not want to think about the emotions that will hit him once the job comes to an end with Tuesday's Concacaf Nations League quarterfinal against Haiti. He preached that it's still business as usual, even as one unusual week comes to a close and another equally unusual week begins.

Industry observers note that after two years of answering questions about Pochettino's future as different European clubs took an interest in his services, his decision last week to join Manchester United finally offered them a semblance of clarity. The task in front of them on Tuesday is a simple one, especially after Saturday's 6-0 win over Haiti in the first leg – play like Pochettino's version of the U.S. team one last time.

"For me, tomorrow is about play[ing] like the tie is 0-0," he said on Monday in his penultimate press conference before returning to England. "I don't want to be disappointed. I don't want to lose the focus. I don't want to be less concentrated … [If] you take the game in a way that claims it's not important tomorrow because it's already done, I think you will pay in the future – that lack of respect to the competition, to the opponent, to the result, to yourself. That is why tomorrow what I want is I'm going to put the best team possible and to perform.".

Pochettino has been hesitant to reflect on his legacy after two years with the USMNT but that has been a common refrain during his tenure, spending just as much time molding the team's mentality in his image as he has their style of play. He leaves behind a mixed track record – results were all over the place in the build-up to the World Cup but it all appeared to come together once the tournament started, only for the U.S. team to fall flat on their faces in a round of 16 exit forever tinged by the Folarin Balogun affair. The stakes are undoubtedly lower against Haiti, the first leg advantage so substantial that the USMNT can probably survive another unimpressive performance before closing the book on the Pochettino years. There's a hint of succession planning in his intends for Tuesday, though, even if those plans are no longer his to execute.

It has been revealed that "What I hope is to create the same link with us, with the new coaches that arrive here," Pochettino said. "It's to create the same link with the players. [It's] become an emotional relationship, that you can find the best for this group of players that have enormous talent … That is an official game and it's the opportunity to keep growing for the future, to settle all the principles and grow and grow and grow.".

According to recent reports, for all his faults and shortcomings, Pochettino does leave the national team in better shape than he found it. Some of it is out of his control – up and comers like Julian Hall, who scored on Saturday and now has four goals in his first five games for the senior team, were very likely poised for success no matter who the USMNT head coach was. After much trial and tribulation, though, he implemented a clear style of play and a cultural shift that several players have championed over the last week. Tuesday's game is ultimately a showcase for the players who will remain long after Pochettino leaves, both on an individual level as they aim to impress whoever takes the helm and as they try to prove a collective point now that the Pochettino years are over. U.S. Soccer's financial might may help sway Pochettino's eventual successor to take the job, no matter who that might be, but there is a pure soccer argument to taking this job.

For perhaps the first time in its modern history, the USMNT can prioritize style of play with their next hire. That's true outside the reported approach for ex-Manchester City manager Pep Guardiola, whose interest in the job is unclear. Pochettino's high-intensity, attack-minded version of the U.S. team suited the players at this year's World Cup and feels especially tailor-made for the rising talents headlined by Cavan Sullivan, the 17-year-old Philadelphia Union attacker who is now MLS' youngest-ever MVP nominee. A strong outing on Tuesday will allow the Pochettino years to look like a stepping stone to an vital newly introduced chapter, one that will hopefully get the best out of the experienced players as well as their younger teammates, no matter who oversees the project.

According to recent reports, as for Pochettino, laying the groundwork for the USMNT's future comes while he focuses on his own. Assistant coach Jesus Perez, goalkeeper coach Toni Jimenez and sports scientist Sebastiano Pochettino departed for Manchester after Saturday's win over Haiti at Miami's Nu Stadium, filling in the gaps before Pochettino departs Cincinnati on Wednesday to begin his newly introduced role. The rest of his coaching staff will stay in Ohio to finish out the international break with the USMNT before traveling alongside Pochettino.

Two years removed from starting a latest job with a short runway, Pochettino will do so again at United. The earliest he can oversee his first training session with United is Thursday, three days before an all-crucial clash with Liverpool. The longtime London resident, who previously coached Tottenham Hotspur and Chelsea, insists he will not be out of the loop when he finally makes his Premier League return.

Recent findings suggest that "For me, it's not difficult," he stated of the quick turnaround. "I think we are well prepared to switch quick to like a player, from the national team to the clubs, from one game that you don't play well to another that you need to be ready again, from one action to the next action. I think we are well-prepared and then all the experience from the past, I think, helps us to be focused in the priority of the moment that demands that business. Today is to be focusing here in Cincinnati for the game against Haiti tomorrow but for sure, in the moment that game [finishes], we are going to start to be 100% focused in our next project … We watch soccer every day, all the leagues and we are always because that is our passion, our passion. We know the team [very well]. We know every single team [very well] and I think we don't need to match the preparation about the opponent. The most notable [thing] is to know the details about our players, our staff, our culture, our identity and from there, to improve but now we are focusing [on] that game and we want to finish well tomorrow.".

A large task awaits Pochettino at United, who are at the moment in the relegation zone with just one win from their opening 10 league games of the season.

Diego Kochen shows poise in USMNT net as young goalkeeper stakes claim to starting job

📅 17 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (804 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks.
  • During Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake.
  • Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be important for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Historically, goalkeeper has been a position of strength for the United States men's national team, to the extent that during the time of Tim Howard and Brad Guzan, both were playing Premier League soccer, but only one could start between the sticks. Things have changed since then, with numerous keepers coming through the ranks over the years, with most playing domestically or sitting on the bench for stronger European sides. However, that could be coming to an end for the team.

During Mauricio Pochettino's tenure, Matt Freese has been his starting keeper, taking over during the Gold Cup and starting every game that he was available for until the September/October international window, when Pochettino used Diego Kochen and Brian Schwake. Kochen, who is playing his first season of first-team soccer at Lyngby in Denmark (where center back Neil Pierre also got his first taste of senior soccer), got the clean sheet against Mexico during that camp and turned that into a start against Haiti in Concacaf Nations League play in his native Miami, setting the USMNT up well to advance to the semifinals of the tournament.

Following that match, Kochen acknowledged that the USMNT squad has done a lot to put him in this position, and he'll know that even if Pochettino won't be the manager choosing the lineups, performances like this one will be important for how the USMNT keeper picture looks moving forward.

"I feel like I've grown quite a lot," Kochen mentioned following the match, reflecting on his adjustment to the national team. "I'm getting used to competing at the international level, but I've just got to give it to my team because they've been unbelievable. They make it so easy to just come out here and play free and be me, so without them, this wouldn't be possible.".

His growth is evident; one of the first things that comes to mind when watching the 20-year-old is his poise. Kochen had the ball at his feet plenty, completing all 20 of his passes to help send the attack on its way, and also made the two saves that he needed to on a mostly quiet night. His age also demonstrated when Haiti scored with him out of position, a goal that was called back for offside, but you take the good with the bad for young players because that's a learning moment, and as he earns more reps at the senior level, those are the kind of mistakes that can be ironed out.

"I'm not saying he hasn't played games in Barcelona, but at the senior level, every game he plays, he gets better and better and better," one of Kochen's coaches, Andreas Bjelland, told CBS Sports. "Because understanding the full-pitch play, and not only being on the line, just taking shots, and being a training goalie, but now he's playing for points every week. He's growing as a player, as a person, and as somebody we can trust more and more in the stuff we do. So it's nice to see that it has come to this ... It's quite impressive.".

You can't teach poise, and spending more than five years in the Barcelona system highlights in how Kochen carries himself. It's becoming more common in American soccer for young players to test themselves abroad or to get into Major League Soccer teams at a younger age, and when they succeed, it goes a long way developmentally, as Kochen's case shows.

According to recent reports, "He is a person who trusts himself a lot. That's also why he's a good goalie, that at such a young age he hasn't that significant of a doubt of himself," Mikkel Jespersen, Lyngby's other coach noted. "He knows what he's capable of doing, and that's really important as a goalie: that you trust yourself and know what things you are doing is something that can succeed in a longer period.".

It has been revealed that while it's unknown what the next USMNT manager will value in a keeper, being able to perform in an uncertain environment with your coach having one foot out the door is something that will go a long way for Kochen's chances. In keeper terms, Kochen has plenty of time ahead of him, as players at his position regularly play until their late 30s or early 40s, so if he can continue this trajectory, the question of who protects the net could be solved for the foreseeable future.

Industry observers note that of course, that's a lot of projecting, but when the next generation of the USMNT is developing at an astounding rate, it's only natural to think about where players like Kochen could end up. Doing this in only his first season of professional soccer is already impressive, but the best is yet to come.

#139958. Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 • ⏱️ 5m • 📚 Deep Dive (1066 w)
📖 Baca
General ⚖️ Neutral 🌐 Dw ↗ Open Full Page

Can a 'coalition of the willing' create momentum for a fossil fuel phaseout?

📅 16 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 5 min read (1066 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Dw

⏱️ ~5 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • This time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal.
  • But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.
  • According to recent reports, as a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

This time last year, as negotiations at the UN COP climate summit in Brazil entered crunch time, there was hope that governments would agree on a clear roadmap for phasing out oil, gas and coal. More than 80 countries backed the idea.

But instead, after opposition from oil-producing states such as Russia and Saudi Arabia, the conference wrapped up with a watered-down final agreement that did not explicitly mention fossil fuels.

According to recent reports, as a compromise, summit host Brazil offered to produce a "voluntary" roadmap. At the same time, a group of 57 countries frustrated with the deadlock at the consensus-based UN talks decided to form a "coalition of the willing" to accelerate the fossil fuel exit outside the COP framework.

They held their own summit in April in Santa Marta, Colombia — the first such conference to specifically focus on implementing the transition away from fossil fuels (referred to as TAFF).

Co-hosted by Colombia and the Netherlands, the Santa Marta conference brought together countries including Canada, Norway, Brazil, Nigeria, Mexico, Australia and Germany, as well as highly climate-vulnerable states such as Vanuatu.

The idea was for governments to start developing national roadmaps and working out how to restructure their financial and trade systems to wean themselves off polluting energy sources — an incredibly complicated undertaking, particularly for developing countries dependent on revenue from fossil fuel exports.

Part of their discussions focused on cutting subsidies for oil, coal and gas, as well as supporting people whose livelihoods rely on the fossil fuel industry to find new forms of income.

A little over six months on from the Santa Marta meeting, representatives from almost 200 countries are holding talks in Antalya, Turkey, as part of the latest UN climate conference.

According to recent reports, countries agreed for the first time in 2023 to transition away from fossil fuels — the main driver behind rising global temperatures. But summits since then have failed to pin down how to implement that pledge.

It's not yet clear whether the Santa Marta coalition will influence ambition at this year's COP.

"I think it's more of a long-term game," stated Chetna Hareesh Kumar, a climate policy analyst at the Berlin-based research organization NewClimate Institute.

Sources indicate that she indicates it's too soon to expect the coalition to have an influence on the negotiations but adds that that could change at future COPs. The grouping could bring more nations on board if, for example, it indicates it can be truly inclusive, address the needs of different types of countries and show that a transition is feasible.

One role the group is playing, according to Alexandra Scott, a senior climate diplomacy adviser at Italian climate change think tank ECCO, is "keeping up the political momentum," and showing "that there is this huge group of countries who really want to accelerate this transition away from fossil fuels.".

She indicates it's also building an invaluable "cadre of knowledge" on how to develop national TAFF plans and deal with barriers individual countries face — like how to secure funding for the infrastructure investments needed for the energy transition.

The Santa Marta group is "really answering a lot of the questions that countries have always had on how on earth do we even start to transition our whole economy off fossil fuels?" Scott mentioned.

This expertise being shared and tested in practice can show what such a transformation could look like and the knowledge brought into COP, added Scott.

Sources indicate that since the Santa Marta conference, Germany, France and the Netherlands have released national intends to phase out fossil fuels. While the plans contain no new commitments, experts see them as a positive first step.

Industry observers note that kumar says more countries could announce similar prepares just ahead of the second TAFF summit in Tuvalu next year. Finland presented its TAFF roadmap in the first week of COP, but analysts do not expect many more countries to follow suit soon.

Another potential boost that could get momentum going is Brazil's recently published global roadmap to transition away from fossil fuels, promised at last year's COP.

It has been revealed that the nearly 200-page document seeks to serve as a toolkit for countries shifting from fossil fuels to renewable energy, such as wind and solar. It envisages countries making a phased transition between 2028 and 2033.

The aim, Ana Toni, CEO of last year's COP, told AP, is to break down the transition into "smaller actionable solutions" and help countries make practical progress.

According to recent reports, the roadmap suggests measures tailored to each country's circumstances, including dependence on fossil fuel and financial capacities. "Levers" it proposes include reducing fossil fuel subsidies, expanding renewable energy and cutting methane emissions.

Kumar called it a "customizable" approach that allows every country to take action, regardless of its situation. "The question really is now what countries do with it and how much momentum they can generate," she added.

This year's climate change summit in Turkey — taking place after a series of deadly heat waves in Europe and a glacier collapse in Nepal that killed more than 1,400 people — isn't expected to result in any big announcements about fossil fuels.

In a recent development, global renewable energy capacity has surged in recent years, making up a third of the world's power generation for the first time in 2025. But many countries still rely on coal, oil and gas.

A database compiled by the German environmental organization Urgewald reveals that most oil and gas companies worldwide, among them QatarEnergy, Saudi Aramco and Russia's Gazprom, are exploring or developing new reserves.

Meanwhile, subsidies for fossil fuels amount to around $920 billion (around €830 billion) per year, according to data from the OECD, but that number is falling.

One issue Turkey is pushing at the COP conference is electrification. It's calling on countries to endorse the goal of 35% of final energy consumption coming from electricity by 2035 — up from around 20% today.

The pledge has drawn criticism from some circles, though, for leaving open whether that additional electricity needs to come from clean sources.

Ideally, Kumar stated, electrification would be powered by renewables and tied to a goal of phasing out polluting fossil fuels.

"If something like that could make it to the final text, that would be a really good sign for momentum.".

UEFA Women's Champions League Matchday 5: Live stream, schedule what to know as league phase nears end

📅 18 Nov 2026 | ⏱️ 4 min read (874 words, 📚 Deep Dive) | Source: Cbssports

⏱️ ~4 mins left to finish
📖 0% read
💡 Key Takeaways
  • Recent findings suggest that there is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League.
  • Recent findings suggest that OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment.
  • The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.
📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

Recent findings suggest that there is no more room for error in the 2026-27 UEFA Women's Champions League. After four matchdays, the league phase has been whittled down to only two games left for each of the 18 clubs, and the margin between a bye into the quarterfinals and an extra round of knockout playoffs in February will come down to dwindling points.

Recent findings suggest that OL Lyonnes rule the league phase at the moment. They top the tournament table with ten points, level with FC Barcelona but with a superior goal difference. Just behind the two Champions League contenders are Bayern Munich and Arsenal, with Chelsea FC and Manchester City creeping closer to the top four. Out of the 18 clubs competing, only four will earn direct berths to the quarterfinals, and eight will compete for a future spot alongside them.

The final six clubs with the least amount of points will see their Champions League dream end, so matchday 5 will be a crucial turning point for several teams.

Fighting for top spot positioning will be Arsenal and OL Lyonnes, and Chelsea against Paris Saint-Germain. HB Koge, Roma, and tournament debutants Inter Milan are level on four points and need to be in full urgency mode if they're to leapfrog and remain in contention for future rounds.

Here's what to watch on Matchday 5:.

Recent findings suggest that wednesday, Nov. 18BK Hacken vs. Manchester City, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)Real Madrid vs. Inter, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Chelsea vs. Paris Saint-Germain, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Juventus vs. OH Leuven, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Thursday, Nov. 19 Austria Wien vs. Bayern Munich, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)   Paris FC vs. HB Koge, 12:45 p.m. (Paramount+)  Arsenal vs. OL Lyonnes, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)   Barcelona vs. Servette, 3 p.m. (Paramount+)  Benfica vs. Roma, 3 p.m. (Paramount+).

Fans could get a glimpse of a future round when Arsenal take on OL Lyonnes on Thursday. The Gunners now have the tall task of tackling the French giants after battling Barcelona to a 1-1 draw at Camp Nou last week.

According to recent reports, A strong team defensive performance, anchored by goalkeeper Misa Rodriguez against the current title holders, and the inclusion of Frida Maanum in the attack were key difference-makers. Manager Renee Slegers and her side seem to be turning the page, with better results after questionable tactics and player availability raised concerns about the club's earlier performances.

Taking on OL Lyonnes also won't be easy. The top French side has scored 20 goals through four league phase matches, and Marie-Antoinette Katoto leads the competition's Golden Boot race with seven goals. U.S. women's national team defensive midfielder Lily Yohannes is getting more lethal in the tournament and scored in her second consecutive tournament match during OL's 6-0 blowout against Juventus.

Lily Yohannes makes it FOUR 💥The USWNT midfielder has now scored in back-to-back UWCL matches 🇺🇸🔥Stream every UEFA Women’s Champions League game on @paramountplus 📺 pic.twitter.com/9uLM309RM4.

The eight-time Champions League winners will go up against an English club with plenty of momentum following last week's results against Barcelona. The Gunners have more players available to shake things up on the pitch, and Alessia Russo remains a threat after her hat trick against Benfica and has four goals in the league phase.

Chelsea FC will host PSG and the Blues are riding high on stout defensive performances. They co-lead the tournament alongside OL Lyonnes with zero goals conceded through four league phase games.

Industry observers note that the London side will need to be far better in attack if they want to claim being a top contender, though it's not for lack of trying. They're coming off a scoreless draw against BK Hacken, where they recorded a whopping 32 shots but only six attempts on target. U.S. women's national team winger Alyssa Thompson is still a factor with her swift technique and could help stretch PSG's backline, while Wieke Kaptein gets into dangerous spaces. Kaptein created both goals in Chelsea's 2-0 win against Roma, and the Dutch player has one goal and two assists in the tournament.

Industry observers note that PSG's fortunes seem to be turning for the worse after a promising start to the competition. They're in 10th place on the table now with five points and just one win in their last four games. The loss of Sakina Karchaoui with an ankle injury for the remainder of the league phase is a blow to the roster, though Naomie Feller, with two goals and two assists, is a threat for the Parisians.

Recent findings suggest that there are plenty of teams on the lower side of the table and running out of time. Alongside PSG with necessary urgency are Juventus, who were just beaten by OL Lyonnes, 6-0, and face a desperate 17th-place OH Leuven before closing out the league phase against PSG. It makes the penultimate meeting with OH Leuven almost a must win for Juventus, to lessen the stress on the final matchday.

A particularly intriguing matchup between ninth-place Benfica and 12th-place Roma could shake up the league table with a win by either side. If Roma's Kayleigh van Dooren and Alayah Pilgrim stay active on offense again, it could be a tough challenge for Benfica.

📑 Quick Jump: 1. Overview • 2. Key Details • 3. Closing Notes

In a farewell for Mauricio Pochettino before he heads to Manchester United, the United States men's national team were able to defeat Haiti 2-0 on Tuesday night, advancing in the Concacaf Nations League quarterfinals 8-0 on aggregate. Christian Pulisic opened the scoring with a bicycle-kick goal to kick things off, which was the emphatic send-off that was needed prior to Pochettino arriving in Manchester, but the USMNT were able to keep things up in the celebration in Cincinnati.

CHRISTIAN PULISIC GET ON YOUR BIKE‼️#USMNT x @VW pic.twitter.com/Yb3yqXfC33.

Julian Hall followed with a poacher's goal as Weston McKennie played orchestrator, and it continued a theme that whoever ends up taking over the national team will have tough decisions ahead. Folarin Balogun is struggling for minutes with Monaco and is looking to make a move at the end of the season, and Hall has done everything that he can to increase his own standing with five goals in six games for the USMNT.

It has been revealed that the Latest York Red Bulls star has a ways to go considering that he's still only 18 and will need to gain experience against top teams in the world instead of just Haiti, but he also can't ask for a better start than what he has gotten off to. It's why this is such an attractive job for whoever takes over the USMNT. They'll be able to build upon the good that Pochettino has instilled; the talent is there to move the squad forward, and there's plenty to love about the youth of the USMNT.

Industry observers note that and alongside that, Pulisic has essentially screamed don't forget about me. During this camp, the Milan man has followed up on signing a new contract with the club by reaching 35 national team goals, moving into fourth all time for the USMNT over Eric Wynalda. Diego Kochen added to the good vibes with a third straight clean sheet, and Neil Pierre was even able to be cap-tied against the nation that he's also eligible for as the full-circle moments were left and right.

Pulisic, the former 17-year-old phenom, was subbed off for Cavan Sullivan, the current 17-year-old phenom, and while the goal difference may have been larger in the first leg between these sides, this felt like a more measured performance despite the strangeness of Pochettino's assistants heading to United while he managed the squad prior to catching his own charter.

This camp had every chance of being a disaster given the circumstances of Pochettino leaving, but all parties did what was needed during this camp. All dual nationals were capped, including Santiago Castaneda, showing that even on his way out, Pochettino made sure to take care of the future of the federation. On to the next round of the Concacaf Nations League with a latest manager and no complaints with the performance so far for the squad.

In a recent development, it’s a little on-the-nose, but the messaging will only escalate. Soon we find ourselves staring at what appears to be a Ballon d’Or replica, before the director cuts to a moody shot of the footballer from behind as he stares at a wall of photographs.

This came out at the start of the week. Our epic footballer? That would be JJ Gabriel, aged 16 years and one month, still in braces, and potentially the best you’ve not yet seen.

Recent findings suggest that as you have likely heard, he really is that good. And as you will also know, the mechanisms of his exit from United ahead of an imminent deal with Real Madrid have been ugly.

JJ Gabriel, aged 16 years and one month, still in braces, and potentially the best footballer you’ve not yet seen.

The video Gabriel released this week announcing his exit from Manchester United includes signing for the club at the age of 10 alongside Cristiano Ronaldo Jr (Source: Instagram/Jjnr10).

But let’s momentarily keep to that bizarre video, which has been watched almost two million times on Gabriel’s Instagram page, and from there we can raise the question of whoever thought it was a good idea.

Industry observers note that this is where we should introduce Ali Barat, the owner of Epic Sports. He’s a massive fish in the world of football agencies and the 31-second clip was advertising their latest coup: Gabriel had joined his group, which is timely because a move to Real is imminent and that will follow other big deals brokered by Barat.

They include Moises Caicedo to Chelsea for £115million, Noni Madueke to Arsenal for £52m and Dean Huijsen to Bournemouth for £12.6m, then on to Real Madrid for £50m more. He’s a significant figure with a changeable definition of what it means to be understated. Here’s an example from his company’s website: ‘While some agents seek the spotlight, Ali Barat is quietly reshaping the transfer market.’.

Amusingly, it then goes on to describe Barat as a ‘super-agent’ twice in the same paragraph while declaring he is ‘not just closing deals, he is building careers, guiding legacies, and setting the standard for a upcoming era of football representation’.

Recent findings suggest that the ‘quiet’ part was possibly lost along the way. But ‘legacy’ is the word among that salad most worthy of fixation, because Gabriel has been steered to a series of pivotal decisions at an incredibly young age.

He is yet to play a single minute of competitive senior football but he is clear on what he wishes to become. Earlier this month, his handlers felt it prudent to place him in an interview with the Madrid-based newspaper Marca and Gabriel stated: ‘My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or.’.

Fair enough. He’s a teenager aiming high. Is it wise to say so? Maybe not, but he’s 16. Barat, the super-agent, has no such excuse. He’s 30 years older than his client and saw no harm in a video that invoked the Ballon d’Or to peddle an academy kid.

In a recent development, there’s less ambiguity in the wisdom of what Barat has done there. It reeks. It carries the stench of an agent who evidently doesn’t mind so much if the labels attached to Gabriel today stick for the remainder of his career.

Earlier this month, his handlers felt it prudent to place him in an interview with the Madrid-based newspaper Marca and Gabriel said: ‘My dream is to win a Ballon d'Or’.

Gabriel's representative Ali Barat, who is 30 years older than his client and saw no harm in a video that invoked the Ballon d’Or to peddle an academy kid.

In a recent development, I can remember when Mauricio Pochettino once made the blunder of placing Marcus Edwards, a Tottenham wonderkid, into the same sentence as Lionel Messi. His point was that he had some similar movement patterns, but the fact the lad was named mini-Messi in training didn’t help – it was a tag that endured.

Thankfully, Edwards has carved out a respectable career at Burnley via Sporting in Portugal, but Pochettino regretted the words as soon as they left his mouth.

That’s different to designing and releasing a video, of course. That’s different to a process involving some level of sign-off. That’s different to the grubby act of hyping a very young guy to a standard reached by only five Englishmen in history.

Industry observers note that A question at this stage: where was Gabriel’s family when this was being decided? That’s somewhat loaded because there is chatter about how much of the United separation has been driven by Gabriel’s father, Joe O'Cearuill, formerly a professional himself for Brighton, Barnet and the Republic of Ireland.

Recent findings suggest that I’d add that many of those noises have originated from within Carrington. It might simply be the bitter discourse of the jilted. But a recurring sentiment among some United staffers is that the father became difficult during the breakdown in relations.

These are lines we have heard before in football. But for once, United do not appear to have done much wrong. There was genuine care for the player. And if there is one thing they can guarantee, it is that young talents get a good chance, though evidently not enough to please Gabriel’s camp.

A demand for minutes against Azerbaijani side Sabah in the Champions League was a bad look; similar might be mentioned with less force around reports that he changed his name from Joseph Junior Andreou O'Cearuill for commercial reasons, feeding one of those blurry conversations about where the athlete ends and the product begins.

Gabriel’s early days with Epic and Barat and his content wing do not serve much encouragement on that front.

It is worth stating that the teenager at the heart of it all is not considered to be a bad sort. Far from it.

None of his ascent was accompanied by the worrying noises that followed another prodigy in Ravel Morrison – once described by Sir Alex Ferguson as having 'as much natural talent as any youngster we ever signed', but who made all of three League Cup appearances for United before a journeyman career through the Championship, Italy, Mexico, Sweden, the Netherlands, the US and the UAE.

One source has suggested Gabriel even cried when he said his goodbyes back in September.

It might be over-reaching to claim he has left the club against his own better judgment, but there is no doubt he has gambled hugely on Real Madrid.

Trent Alexander-Arnold is pretty handy and has found it tough there; Martin Odegaard is a far closer parallel to Gabriel having moved to Madrid aged 15, and he played 11 games in three seasons.

If the pathway was blocked at United, then what is it at a club who employ Vinicius Junior, Rodrygo, Yan Diomande, Arda Guler, Endrick, Brahim Diaz, Jude Bellingham and Kylian Mbappe in Gabriel's positions?

Sources indicate that A upcoming language and surroundings are large hurdles for a young player, especially one whose ambitions are so public and grand. It won’t be a quiet arrival by any definition, even those found in the quirky dictionary of Ali Barat, and the pressure will be significant.

Welsh Rugby Union's 20,000 reasons to be ashamed.

Among the joys of this job is being present at rare moments of sporting greatness. The Welsh win over the All Blacks last weekend was one such occasion and, for me, it was compounded by a subsequent email from a lovely chap named John Evans, aged 87 and from Tredegar in Blaenau Gwent.

John had watched the game on television, but was part of what must be a dwindling group who could say they were there the last time Wales had beaten Fresh Zealand, at the Arms Park in 1953.

After detailing how he, ‘a small-bottomed outside-half’, had left himself with no view of the pitch at the back of the stand, John went on to recall that the crowd around him and a friend ‘decided to pass us over everyone’s head back down to the front’. He landed just in time to see Ken Jones score the winning try. His excitement in sharing a memory from 73 years ago was spelled out in block capitals.

One of the consequences of the ongoing shambles at the Welsh Rugby Union is that there were 20,000 empty seats at the Principality Stadium last weekend, mainly due to a combination of apathy and protest. Accordingly, there will be 20,000 fewer people with a great story to tell decades from now. While the WRU ponder their next blunders, they might wish to consider some of the above.

Andoni Iraola looked up to the ceiling of Fenerbahce’s media auditorium as he tried to find the words to describe the madness he had just witnessed.

Recent findings suggest that “Cheap” was his first conclusion, swiftly followed by “messy”; technically, Liverpool’s head coach was right but this was a moment when nobody would have found glitch had he gone further. “Absurd” and “preposterous” would have been more accurate portrayals of this calamity.

Liverpool have won two European trophies in Istanbul, but they do not tend to enjoy visits to Turkey. Roy Hodgson, in August 2010, was the last Anfield manager to oversee a win here and there was an irony that the hero of that night in Trabzon – Dirk Kuyt – masterminded this downfall.

Kuyt, interim head coach, got a remarkable response out of a Fenerbahce team who had amassed 1,086 Premier League appearances between them and he was as giddy as the locals after Mason Greenwood, Archie Brown and substitute Vedat Muriqi scored to give the club a famous night.

Liverpool were meek, naïve, and while the Turkish side danced in the rain on the Asian side of the city, Iraola was left to dissect the most chastening 90 minutes of his short Anfield career.

Recent findings suggest that “It’s frustration because it’s a difficult place to come here and to play,” mentioned Iraola. “During most of the game, we were thinking: ‘OK we can win this one.’ But obviously it hasn’t happened. We conceded, I think, messy goals, especially the first and the third one. The second one is a rebound.”.

It has been revealed that yet it all started so smoothly. For all that Fenerbahce tried to put Liverpool out of their stride with a soundtrack of high-pitched whistling, Iraola’s side kept the ball well and they might have been ahead in the fifth minute but Victor Muñoz and Bradley Barcola, playing as a central striker, erred.

Those who remember Kuyt from his Anfield days 15 years ago will recall a player who never considered any cause to be lost and the Dutchman implored his team to attack the flanks with pace, even earning himself a yellow card at one point. Eventually, the pressure paid off.

Szoboszlai is rapidly becoming an enigma. How can a player with the gift of being able to score goals from the heavens make the mistakes of a weekend amateur? There was no need for him to foul N’Golo Kanté but the error was compounded, Greenwood’s strike deflecting off Jérémy Jacquet.

Since Manchester United felt duty-bound to sell Greenwood in 2024 the former England forward has continued his career away from the Premier League. After leaving Marseille he has found a home in Istanbul where the fans have taken to him and they bellowed his name following the equaliser.

Alisson Becker, wrong-footed by Jacquet’s decision to break off from the wall and turn his body, was livid and rightly so. Liverpool had gone from sublime (in patches) to ridiculous and the passage of play up to the interval was hugely uncomfortable.

According to recent reports, would things settle down after the break? Not a bit of it. Liverpool, worryingly for Iraola, could not stamp any authority and though there was a brief respite when Cody Gakpo and Alexander Isak combined after being introduced as substitutes, the lead felt as sustainable as a snowball in a sauna.

Andoni Iraola states he will not waste any more time thinking about the penalty Liverpool were denied against Arsenal and won’t seek an explanation from Pro Ref. There was a significant fallout following the 1-0 loss at Anfield on Sunday with many judges believing Stuart Attwell, who was VAR, should have consulted match official Andy Madley to highlight an obvious pull by Jurrien Timber that prevented Alexander Isak heading a Bradley Barcola cross.

Liverpool’s head coach explained in the heat of the moment that he would tell his players to go down if they felt contact in the area and Cody Gakpo, the Netherlands international, explained last night in Istanbul it was a message the squad had taken on board.

“As a team, we play pretty fair – maybe we should dive some more like the gaffer said,” Gakpo, who also had claims to be awarded a penalty against Arsenal, explained. “On both occasions you could have given a penalty or a foul, but they decided not. We have to live with the decision. That’s it.”.

Industry observers note that but as angry as he was with the situation, Iraola has drawn a line on the matter. He is not going to seek out Pro Ref for a discussion – even though he feels a number of decisions have gone against Liverpool this season – and is channelling his energy into other situations.

Iraola said: “I didn’t ask for an explanation and I haven’t received an explanation, no. I told you what you I think about the plays but, honestly, I don’t have the time to [speak to Pro Ref]. I have been preparing for Fenerbahce. It is just two days between games so I have just been focusing on this game and the opposition and how to prepare the team.”.

Liverpool have made the long trip to Turkey to take on Fenerbahce on matchday four of the Champions League.

Sources indicate that liverpool enter this fixture having won all three Champions League matches thus far, beating Atletico Madrid, LASK and Villarreal to make it nine points from nine for Andoni Iraola’s side. Liverpool’s five-game unbeaten streak was ended by Arsenal in the league on Sunday. They return to the city where the club enjoyed one of their most memorable nights, beating AC Milan in the Champions League final 21 years ago.

Sources indicate that “Istanbul is always going to be very special for Liverpool,” Iraola said. “It is difficult to find a more key night. Tomorrow [tonight] it won’t be easy, you talk about statistics, especially English teams playing here. They have very good players and a very good squad, they know how to play in this competition. We have to start strong in the game. It is very early in the season to establish comparisons. We want to continue how we have done in the Champions League, three games and nine points, it is a good chance to get to 12 points and then finish in the top eight. Champions League away is very difficult.”.

In addition to the long-term absentees Hugo Ekitike, Conor Bradley and Giovanni, both Ryan Gravenberch and Jeremie Frimpong have missed the trip to Turkey.

According to recent reports, fenerbahce have made a slow start to their Champions League campaign, taking just two points from their opening three fixtures. They have drawn twice against Roma and Slavia Prague at home whilst they suffered a heavy 6-0 loss at Aston Villa. Former Liverpool forward Dirk Kuyt has been appointed their interim coach following the resignation of Ismail Kartal following their recent defeat to arch rivals Galatasaray just over a week ago.

Sources indicate that “It is a great opportunity for us to show what we can do,” Kuyt noted. “It is also a great opportunity for me, a game between two teams that are very important to me. We have a very good blueprint, and we have to believe in this plan. No-one who loves Fenerbahce is happy with the current situation, but this is a huge opportunity. We have players who have won the Champions League and the World Cup.”.

They come into tonight’s match having lost back-to-back league games since drawing against Slavia Prague on matchday three of the Champions League. They have plenty of former Premier League players in their ranks, including Ederson, N’Golo Kante and Romelu Lukaku.
